item.title: Bangladesh clothing factories close as workers strike for higher pay
item.description: Garment factories in Bangladesh have shut down as workers strike demanding a monthly minimum wage of 30,000 taka (£182).
item.content:encoded:
Clothing factories across Bangladesh have shut down after workers went on strike demanding a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka, equivalent to about £182.

  • Workers strike demanding 30,000 taka monthly minimum wage
  • Clothing factories shut down due to strike action
  • Demand equals approximately £182 per month

Source: BBC News

item.title: Suspected China spy linked to Nvidia ex-boss left in 2025
item.description: Megaspeed says a suspected China spy linked to Nvidia's former boss left in 2025, as the Nvidia scandal raises questions over AI chips reaching China.
item.content:encoded:
Megaspeed says a suspected China spy linked to Nvidia's former boss left in 2025. The Nvidia scandal has raised questions over whether advanced AI chips ended up in China despite US restrictions. The source gives no further details on the case.

  • Megaspeed says a suspected China spy linked to Nvidia's ex-boss left in 2025.
  • The Nvidia scandal raises questions over advanced AI chips reaching China.
  • The concern exists despite US restrictions on such chips.
  • The source gives no further details about the case.

Source: BBC News

item.title: RBI to auction 91-day, 182-day and 364-day Treasury Bills on Nov 18
item.description: The Reserve Bank of India will auction three Treasury Bills worth a total of ₹23,000 crore on November 18, 2026, with settlement on November 19.
item.content:encoded:
The Reserve Bank of India has announced an auction of three Government of India Treasury Bills on November 18, 2026, totalling ₹23,000 crore. The 91-day and 182-day bills are notified at ₹8,000 crore each, and the 364-day bill at ₹7,000 crore. Settlement is on November 19, 2026.

  • The 91-day and 182-day bills are notified at ₹8,000 crore each.
  • The 364-day bill is notified at ₹7,000 crore, taking the total to ₹23,000 crore.
  • Bids will be submitted electronically on the RBI's E-Kuber system on November 18.
  • Retail investors can bid non-competitively, capped at 5 percent of the notified amount.
  • Successful bidders must pay on November 19, 2026.

Source: RBI
